name: NeuroCanvas
tagline: Draw a digit, watch a neural network think
problem: Students meet neural networks as model.fit(): a black box
Backprop, activations and failure modes stay invisible
Deep-learning tutorials assume GPUs, cloud notebooks and internet
Labs with weak Wi-Fi cannot run AI-literacy sessions at all

stats.label: students in Indian higher education (AISHE 2021-22, approx.)
GPUs, installs or internet NeuroCanvas needs
weights you can watch, every one written in plain Python

solution: Draw a digit: probabilities, neurons and saliency update live
Explain mode walks forward pass and backprop with your numbers
Train a fresh network live; teach it your own handwriting
Pure-Python MLP, hand-derived backprop, runs offline on any laptop

features.title: Live prediction
features.desc: 10-class bars update as you draw, about 2 ms per forward + backward pass

features.title: Inside the network
features.desc: Every neuron's activation, strongest connections, top voters, weight images

features.title: Saliency overlay
features.desc: Gradient of the winning score per pixel, glowing on your own strokes

features.title: Explain mode
features.desc: 11 steps from pixels to softmax to backprop to one SGD step, real numbers

features.title: Live training lab
features.desc: Tune lr, neurons, layers, data; watch loss curves and filters evolve

features.title: Teach it
features.desc: Label your drawings, fine-tune with replay, measure fixes vs forgetting

architecture: Browser (vanilla JS + SVG/canvas) -> drawing pad, MNIST-style preprocessing
app.py ThreadingHTTPServer -> JSON API, validation, static files
render + templates -> deterministic synthetic digit generator
mlp + train -> MLP, backprop, SGD with momentum, L2
live + teach -> background trainer, fine-tuning with replay
algorithms: Stroke templates + elastic warp + affine – synthetic handwriting
Bounding-box fit + centre-of-mass shift – MNIST-style preprocessing
Backpropagation + mini-batch SGD with momentum, He init, L2
Gradient saliency and gradient x activation – explanations
Replay fine-tuning – learn new styles without forgetting
tech: Python 3 stdlib only (http.server, math, random, gzip, json)
Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, inline SVG and canvas, no CDN
6,000-image dataset in 0.8 MB, trained weights in 160 KB
unittest: 50 tests incl. finite-difference gradient check
innovation: Every number is inspectable: no framework hides the maths
Explanations use the actual activations of your drawing
Shows failure honestly: confident mistakes, forgetting, divergence
Starts in 0.1 s on a cheap laptop with Wi-Fi off

results.label: mouse-drawn digits in a real browser; 60/60 after teaching 3
